sn12.60:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Kurus, where there was a town of the Kurus named Kammasadamma.
sn12.60:1.2: Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to him:
sn12.60:1.3: “It is wonderful, venerable sir! It is amazing, venerable sir!
sn12.60:1.4: This dependent origination is so deep and so deep in implications, yet to me it seems as clear as clear can be.”
sn12.60:2.2: This dependent origination is deep and deep in implications.
sn12.60:2.3: It is because of not understanding and not penetrating this Dhamma, Ānanda, that this generation has become like a tangled skein, like a knotted ball of thread, like matted reeds and rushes, and does not pass beyond the plane of misery, the bad destinations, the nether world, saṁsara.
sn12.60:3.1: “Ānanda, when one dwells contemplating gratification in things that can be clung to, craving increases.
sn12.60:3.2: With craving as condition, clinging comes to be….
sn12.60:3.6: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.60:4.1: “Suppose, Ānanda, there was a great tree,
sn12.60:4.2: and all its roots going downwards and across would send the sap upwards.
sn12.60:4.3: Sustained by that sap, nourished by it, that great tree would stand for a very long time.
sn12.60:4.4: So too, when one lives contemplating gratification in things that can be clung to, craving increases….
sn12.60:4.7: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.60:5.1: “When, Ānanda, one dwells contemplating danger in things that can be clung to, craving ceases.
sn12.60:5.2: With the cessation of craving comes cessation of clinging….
sn12.60:5.4: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.60:6.1: “Suppose, Ānanda, there was a great tree.
sn12.60:6.2: Then a man would come along bringing a shovel and a basket.
sn12.60:6.3: He would cut down the tree at its foot …
sn12.60:6.4: he would winnow the ashes in a strong wind or let them be carried away by the swift current of a river.
sn12.60:6.7: Thus that great tree would be cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated so that it is no more subject to future arising.
sn12.60:6.8: “So too, Ānanda, when one dwells contemplating danger in things that can be clung to, craving ceases.
sn12.60:6.9: With the cessation of craving comes cessation of clinging;
sn12.60:6.10: with the cessation of clinging, cessation of existence;
sn12.60:6.11: with the cessation of existence, cessation of birth;
sn12.60:6.12: with the cessation of birth, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair cease.
sn12.60:6.13: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”
